claims.title: The kingdom of Saba flourishes at Marib
claims.summary: Saba, the biblical Sheba, emerged as the dominant South Arabian kingdom, with its capital at Marib controlling the lucrative caravan trade in frankincense and myrrh.

sources.label: Saba (ancient kingdom, Arabia)
Marib: Yemen, Dam, and History

claims.title: Construction of the Great Dam of Marib
claims.summary: The Sabaeans built the Great Dam of Marib to harness the seasonal floods of the Wadi Adhanah, irrigating a vast oasis and underpinning the kingdom's wealth for over a thousand years.

claims.title: Rise of the Himyarite kingdom
claims.summary: The Himyarites rose in the southern highlands and gradually absorbed Saba, Qataban and Hadramawt, uniting much of South Arabia under a single dynasty.

sources.label: Yemen: History (ancient kingdoms, Islam, the imamate, unification and war)
The Kingdoms of Aksum and Himyar (World History, Volume 1)

claims.title: Aksumite conquest and the viceroy Abraha
claims.summary: An Ethiopian (Aksumite) invasion overthrew the Himyarite kingdom; the Christian viceroy Abraha later ruled from Yemen before the Sasanian Persians seized the region around 570.

claims.title: Yemen embraces Islam
claims.summary: Yemen adopted Islam in the 7th century, within the Prophet Muhammad's lifetime, and Sanaa became a major centre for the spread of the new faith in the 7th and 8th centuries.

sources.label: Yemen: History (ancient kingdoms, Islam, the imamate, unification and war)

claims.title: Founding of the Zaidi imamate
claims.summary: The scholar Yahya ibn al-Husayn, invited from Medina to arbitrate tribal disputes around Saada, founded the Zaidi imamate, binding the northern highlands to Zaidi Shia Islam for over a thousand years.

sources.label: Yemen: History (ancient kingdoms, Islam, the imamate, unification and war)

claims.title: Ottomans claim Yemen
claims.summary: From around the 1520s the Ottoman Empire asserted control over Yemen's ports and lowlands, contesting the highlands with the Zaidi imams in a struggle that recurred for centuries.

claims.title: Zabid recognised as a centre of Islamic learning
claims.summary: The historic town of Zabid, capital of Yemen under the Rasulids and a celebrated centre of Islamic scholarship from the 13th to 15th centuries, was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

claims.title: Britain captures Aden
claims.summary: The British East India Company seized the port of Aden, establishing a coaling station on the route to India that grew into one of the world's busiest ports after the Suez Canal opened in 1869.

claims.title: Ottoman return to the highlands
claims.summary: The Ottomans reoccupied northern Yemen in the 19th century, meeting sustained resistance from the Zaidi tribes and imams of the mountainous interior.

claims.summary: A United Nations Development Programme report projected that the war would have caused roughly 377,000 deaths by the end of 2021, most from indirect causes such as hunger and disease.

claims.title: UN-mediated nationwide truce
claims.summary: A two-month UN-brokered truce took effect on 2 April 2022, easing fighting, allowing fuel ships into Hodeidah and flights from Sanaa; it was extended and, though it later lapsed, largely held.
